text.p: The lira closed weaker at 105,280 against the dollar on Monday after Friday's 104,160 due to a sharply higher dollar/mark parity and banks' dollar demand despite central bank's minor intervention.
Bankers said the markets were tense after S&P's downgrading of Turkey's long-term currency rating on Friday.
The S&P cut Turkey's long-term foreign currency debt rating to "single B" from "single B-plus" and reaffirmed its "single-B" rating of Turkey's short-term foreign currency debt.
It said the downgrade reflected worsening fiscal and debt service pressures as the coalition government failed to show the will to implement reforms to tackle the growing budget deficit.

The lira dived to a low of 105,400 in late morning on banks' dollar demand and the U.S. currency's gains against mark in world markets. The central bank sold dollars for lira to banks in late morning and all afternoon to curb dollar demand after which the lira firmed to 105,280.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 105,000 lira at the opening, after Friday's 104,000 lira close, and raised it to 105,050 as the dollar rose abroad.

The money market opened with a 24.8 trillion lira surplus. Overnight money traded at between 75 and 77.75 percent in the day and the central bank injected 14.6 trillion lira at 78 percent overnight at close.
It had drained 12.6 trillion overnight at 57 percent on Friday when the average money rate was 59.98.

The central bank lent banks 26.2 trillion lira via t/n value deals at 74 percent, little changed from the 25.5 trillion lira it injected on Friday. It also lent 300 billion lira at 75 percent via t/w value deals.
Yields on the bond market rose by between two and three points across the board on a selling spree triggered by the S&P move.

The average yield on the most heavily traded September 3, 1997 paper firmed to 115.86 from Friday's 113.62 percent. The second most active June 4, 1997, paper yielded 114.95, up from Friday's 112.70 percent average.
The central bank said the Treasury would auction the first ever 13-month bonds on Tuesday with Wednesday value when 76.2 trillion lira will be cashed in.
